newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - March 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - March 4.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Tuesday:

* Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori paid a surprise visit to Cuba and reached an agreement with Cuban leader Fidel Castro for Cuba to give asylum to the Marxist rebels holding 72 hostages at the Japanese Embassy in Lima, Peru.

* Despite multi-million dollar anti-drug efforts and a declining market, cocaine has remained a resilient drug, sustained by the economics of cheap labour, enormous profits and demand from a base of addicted users.

* Vice President Al Gore acknowledged that he made telephone calls from his White House office seeking campaign contributions for his party, but insisted such actions were not wrong, much less illegal.
* The death toll from tornadoes and floods that have torn a path through eight U.S. states from Texas to West Virginia rose to 44 and included 24 deaths in Arkansas, the hardest hit state.

* Russia has concluded that the expansion of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation is inevitable and is now trying to contain NATO with efforts such as a new, NATO-Russian council that would give Russia a voice on European security affairs.

* China's exports rose to $151 billion in 1996, a thirtyfold increase in 20 years, and during some months last year, China surpassed Japan as the country with the greatest trade surplus with the United States. Though some may question whether China will threaten American jobs, crucial differences mean China has a long way to go before its gains translate into the loss of U.S. jobs.
